title: Section 6 treatment search and selection
description: Artifact contracts and complete mechanism typings for Section 6 complete-treatment construction, search, arbitration, selection, and repair. The records assert candidate semantic compatibility only, not bindings, architecture, or a selected pipeline.

artifactTypes.label: Finite treatment tuple factors
artifactTypes.description: Finite background, surface, foreground, accent, and field-state alternatives with declared factor membership. This is a factor domain, not a domain of already constructed complete tuples.
sourceNotes: research/v4/MECHANISMS.md:1334-1341 and :1352-1358 distinguish finite tuple factors from feasible complete treatments.
provenanceNotes: Factor identity and finite cardinality must be retained; an empty factor is explicit rather than omitted.

artifactTypes.label: Complete-treatment legality configuration
artifactTypes.description: Explicit settings for role legality, collapse, field states, gradient endpoints, contrast, and rejection-check order used while constructing internal complete treatments.
sourceNotes: research/v4/MECHANISMS.md:1334-1338 names the jointly evaluated legality settings.
provenanceNotes: The configuration identity must travel with constructed domains and reports.

artifactTypes.label: Internal complete treatment
artifactTypes.description: A complete internal background, surface, foreground, accent, and field-state treatment with collapse, lineage, legality, and score data. It is not the exact v3 published Palette contract and carries no product authority.
sourceNotes: research/v2-3/src/internal/palette-core.ts:422-442 defines the historical internal CompletePaletteTreatment shape; research/v3/src/contract/types.ts:326-341 defines a distinct published Palette contract.
provenanceNotes: This type intentionally does not identify artifact.product.ui-palette.v3 and must not be treated as published product output.

artifactTypes.label: Complete-treatment descriptor
artifactTypes.description: One logical descriptor binding an internal complete treatment to field hypothesis, source mode, complete lineage, canonical key, and evaluation evidence. Distinct descriptors may describe the same internal treatment.
sourceNotes: research/v2-3/src/internal/candidate-domain.ts:23-28 and candidate-materialization.ts:11-15 retain logical descriptors separately from canonical treatments.
provenanceNotes: Descriptor multiplicity and lineage survive treatment-key equality.

artifactTypes.label: Complete-treatment tuple domain
artifactTypes.description: A declared domain of complete-treatment descriptors and their internal treatments, cardinality, scores, and rejection accounting. State is explicitly nonempty, empty, or infeasible; empty membership is not confused with a missing artifact.

notes: This inspection-only discriminator makes empty, infeasible, and populated domain states machine-checkable without defining the complete runtime payload schema.
Only the declared state discriminator is exposed for graph-level constraint inspection.

sourceNotes: research/v4/MECHANISMS.md:1337-1341, :1475-1478, and :1541-1544 require declared-domain scope and explicit infeasibility.
provenanceNotes: The domain records its construction and policy identities; it is not interchangeable with one descriptor or one selected treatment.

artifactTypes.label: Complete-tuple enumeration report
artifactTypes.description: Cardinality, lineage reconciliation, feasible and rejected counts, and first rejection reasons for a finite enumeration, including explicit empty or infeasible results.
sourceNotes: research/v4/MECHANISMS.md:1337-1338 requires cardinality, full lineage, scores, and rejection reasons.
provenanceNotes: Counts are relative to the supplied finite factor domain and legality configuration.

artifactTypes.label: Exact search objective
artifactTypes.description: Frozen objective definition, direction, arithmetic, and identity against which an exact search result and certificate are meaningful.
sourceNotes: research/v4/MECHANISMS.md:1350-1357 limits exactness to the exact frozen objective supplied.
provenanceNotes: Changing the objective invalidates objective-relative optimality claims.

artifactTypes.label: Deterministic branch order
artifactTypes.description: Explicit total traversal order for branches and tuple factors in an exact search.
sourceNotes: research/v4/MECHANISMS.md:1354-1355 requires deterministic branch order.
provenanceNotes: Order identity supports replay but does not itself rank treatment quality.

artifactTypes.label: Admissible search bounds
artifactTypes.description: Bound functions, validity assumptions, and objective identity used to prune branches without excluding the optimum for that objective.
sourceNotes: research/v4/MECHANISMS.md:1352-1357 makes admissible bound validity load-bearing.
provenanceNotes: A certificate must bind both objective and bound identities.

artifactTypes.label: Objective-relative search certificate
artifactTypes.description: Optimal tuple or explicit empty-domain result, exact objective value when present, visited and pruned counts, and bound witnesses proving optimality only for the bound objective and supplied finite factors.
sourceNotes: research/v4/MECHANISMS.md:1354-1357 requires visited/pruned counts and an objective-relative optimality certificate.
provenanceNotes: The certificate does not claim aesthetic optimality or completeness outside the finite factors.

artifactTypes.label: Selected internal treatment
artifactTypes.description: An internal complete treatment paired with the selector identity and selection basis that elected it. It is not the v3 product Palette and is absent when the accompanying outcome has no selected member.
sourceNotes: Section 6 selector outputs are internal winners or members; research/v3/src/contract/types.ts:326-341 separately defines the exact published Palette.
provenanceNotes: Selection never upgrades this type to artifact.product.ui-palette.v3.

artifactTypes.label: Treatment selection outcome
artifactTypes.description: Explicit selector result state such as selected, empty-domain, no-eligible-member, baseline-retained, or promoted, with selected key and margin when applicable.
sourceNotes: research/v4/MECHANISMS.md:1438-1439, :1490-1491, and the documented empty eligibility risk at :1477 require selection and no-selection states.
provenanceNotes: The outcome carries the selector and input-domain identities; a missing selected treatment is explained by an explicit state.

artifactTypes.label: Pareto quality dimensions
artifactTypes.description: Fixed retained quality dimensions, directions, resolutions, missing-value behavior, and dominance semantics for treatment frontier construction.
sourceNotes: research/v4/MECHANISMS.md:1368-1374 requires a fixed vector of dimensions and resolutions.
provenanceNotes: Omitted dimensions are visible configuration choices, not implicit defaults.

artifactTypes.label: Treatment Pareto subset
artifactTypes.description: The nondominated subset of a named complete-treatment domain under a named partial order. It may be explicitly empty only when the input domain is empty.
sourceNotes: research/v4/MECHANISMS.md:1368-1375 defines retention without winner selection; NATIVE_COMPLETE_PALETTE_PROTOCOL.md:325-333 uses a separate post-admission Pareto subset.
provenanceNotes: A frontier is a subset, not a total ranking or selected winner.

artifactTypes.label: Treatment partial order
artifactTypes.description: Pairwise no-worse, strictly-better, equal, and incomparable relations over a named treatment domain under declared dimensions or blocks. Empty and singleton relations are explicit.
sourceNotes: research/v4/MECHANISMS.md:1368-1375, :1454-1459, and :1521-1531 contain dominance and incomparability rather than complete ordering.
provenanceNotes: Incomparability is preserved and must not be silently linearized.

artifactTypes.label: Pareto retention audit
artifactTypes.description: Per-evaluation Pareto membership, retained frontier identity, and audited pruned rows with their dominators and configured resolutions.
sourceNotes: research/v4/MECHANISMS.md:1372-1377 requires membership flags and audited pruned rows.
provenanceNotes: The report records harmful and protective pruning without asserting selection authority.

artifactTypes.label: Banded comparator policy
artifactTypes.description: Evidence resolutions, quality block order, relational stages, quantization rules, and deterministic fallbacks for a banded treatment comparator.
sourceNotes: research/v4/MECHANISMS.md:1388-1393 and v2-3 winner-scoring.ts:1028-1087 expose the staged comparator policy.
provenanceNotes: All deciding stages and quanta are configuration, not hidden comparator constants.

artifactTypes.label: Treatment total order
artifactTypes.description: A complete deterministic ordering of every member of a named treatment domain, including an explicit empty order for an empty domain. This is distinct from a dominance partial order.
sourceNotes: research/v4/MECHANISMS.md:1390-1391, :1407, and :1558-1560 explicitly require total or deterministic orders.
provenanceNotes: The artifact binds comparator and domain identities and does not imply Pareto dominance.

artifactTypes.label: Treatment ordering trace
artifactTypes.description: Evidence levels, pairwise deciding stage, tie stages, and deterministic fallback trace for a named treatment order; empty orders carry a no-comparison state.
sourceNotes: research/v4/MECHANISMS.md:1390-1391 and :1558-1563 require deciding-stage and tie traces.
provenanceNotes: Trace records why an order was decided without asserting perceptual utility.

artifactTypes.label: Quality exchange rates
artifactTypes.description: Named quality axes, hand weights, signs, normalization, and scalar aggregation formula for weighted treatment quality.
sourceNotes: research/v4/MECHANISMS.md:1405-1410 identifies exchange rates as load-bearing configuration.
provenanceNotes: The artifact identifies the tested scalar formulation; it is not generic aesthetic authority.

artifactTypes.label: Scalar treatment quality evaluations
artifactTypes.description: One scalar per treatment and its constituent weighted contributions under a named exchange-rate configuration, including an explicit empty evaluation set.
sourceNotes: research/v4/MECHANISMS.md:1405-1408 defines the weighted scalar output.
provenanceNotes: The scalar remains tied to its axes and exchange rates.

artifactTypes.label: Global description-length coding model
artifactTypes.description: Research coding model and pricing configuration for roles, collapse, gradients, data fit, and explanation breakdown in a global MDL treatment objective.
sourceNotes: research/v4/MECHANISMS.md:1421-1427 describes the tested coding model and pricing risks.
provenanceNotes: Model and pricing identity must be retained with every cost and optimum.

artifactTypes.label: Description-length selection report
artifactTypes.description: Per-configuration coding cost, global optimum or explicit empty-domain state, and role, collapse, gradient, and data-fit coding breakdown.
sourceNotes: research/v4/MECHANISMS.md:1423-1427 requires one cost, optimum, and coding explanation.
provenanceNotes: A reported optimum is relative to the supplied domain and coding model.

artifactTypes.label: Portfolio member-independent evidence
artifactTypes.description: Evidence computed without reading portfolio member identity, including declared description-length and coverage terms for comparing rival complete extractors.
sourceNotes: research/v4/MECHANISMS.md:1436-1439 requires member-independent evidence.
provenanceNotes: Evidence records its member-independence assumptions and source scope.

artifactTypes.label: Portfolio selection report
artifactTypes.description: Selected member or explicit no-member state, margin, bits and coverage trace, and complete disagreement set for a rival-treatment portfolio.
sourceNotes: research/v4/MECHANISMS.md:1438-1442 names member, margin, trace, and disagreement outputs.
provenanceNotes: The report binds the exact tested selector form and portfolio roster.

artifactTypes.label: Noncompensatory quality blocks
artifactTypes.description: Fixed block definitions, component bars, block order, epsilon rules, and incomparable-state semantics for incumbent-relative arbitration.
sourceNotes: research/v4/MECHANISMS.md:1454-1463 makes block definitions, bars, and order explicit.
provenanceNotes: Omitted and redundant blocks remain inspectable policy choices.

artifactTypes.label: Noncompensatory survivor subset
artifactTypes.description: Candidates that survive every applicable noncompensatory block comparison, including an explicit empty subset when all candidates fail or the input is empty.
sourceNotes: research/v4/MECHANISMS.md:1458-1459 requires survivors separately from pairwise verdicts.
provenanceNotes: Survival is relative to the supplied blocks and does not imply a total order or winner.

artifactTypes.label: Noncompensatory arbitration report
artifactTypes.description: Pairwise block verdicts, first deciding block, failed bars, and explicit equal or incomparable states for every audited candidate comparison.
sourceNotes: research/v4/MECHANISMS.md:1458-1463 requires first deciding block and incomparable states.
provenanceNotes: No surplus in one block is represented as compensation for a failed binding block.

artifactTypes.label: Emergency treatment eligibility diagnosis
artifactTypes.description: Optional diagnosis of the exact declared one-color black or white emergency form, including eligibility, reason, supported-pair count, maximum supported contrast, and threshold.
sourceNotes: research/v2-3/src/internal/source-eligibility.ts:119-171 defines the exact optional emergency diagnosis checked by source eligibility.
provenanceNotes: Absence means no emergency basis was supplied; it does not mean emergency eligibility.

artifactTypes.label: Source-eligible treatment subset
artifactTypes.description: The subset having at least one descriptor with complete ordinary source lineage or the exact declared emergency basis. The subset may explicitly be empty.
sourceNotes: research/v4/MECHANISMS.md:1473-1478 and source-eligibility.ts:218-261 define descriptor-based subset filtering.
provenanceNotes: Eligibility proves custody consistency, not semantic belonging or quality.

artifactTypes.label: Source-lineage eligibility report
artifactTypes.description: Per-descriptor field, role, representative, binding, source-connection, and canonical-key booleans plus per-candidate basis, counts, and ineligible diagnostics.
sourceNotes: research/v4/MECHANISMS.md:1473-1478 and source-eligibility.ts:22-50 define the required booleans, basis, and counts.
provenanceNotes: An empty eligible subset is reported rather than converted into an unrestricted winner.

artifactTypes.label: Gradient transition publication decision
artifactTypes.description: Accepted transition hypothesis IDs, eligibility, midpoint disposition, exact stop-path presence, or explicit no-midpoint and legal flat fallback with rejection provenance.
sourceNotes: Earned publication and fallback states are specified in research/v4/MECHANISMS.md:1158-1164.
provenanceNotes: A flat fallback must remain distinguishable from a missing computation and retain the rejected path identities.

artifactTypes.label: Ordered identity obligation
artifactTypes.description: One source-connected, materially distinct, non-field-owned family obligation with priority, direction, and evidence provenance.
sourceNotes: The base list has four seats and post-cap major-family and chromatic reservations can increase the output to six.
provenanceNotes: An obligation is a retention hypothesis, not human semantic truth or final role authority.

artifactTypes.label: Transition promotion objective
artifactTypes.description: Objective revision, promotion ordering, decisive coverage definition, quality envelope utility, tolerance, and both baseline-relative loss budgets.
sourceNotes: research/v4/MECHANISMS.md:1487-1494 and transition-promotion.ts:15-24 require fixed objective and distinct quality-envelope baselines.
provenanceNotes: The two envelope baselines and shared budget are named so they cannot drift.

artifactTypes.label: Transition promotion report
artifactTypes.description: Per-candidate source connection, earned transition, obligation coverage, quality-envelope, and promotion-eligibility fields plus baseline, promoted key, or explicit empty-domain state.
sourceNotes: research/v4/MECHANISMS.md:1490-1494 and transition-promotion.ts:26-41 define per-candidate promotion diagnostics.
provenanceNotes: Baseline retention and actual promotion are distinct states.

artifactTypes.label: Artwork chromatic gamut
artifactTypes.description: Source-bound chromatic mass by hue direction, total mass, pixel counts, and achievable coverage ceiling for a declared number of treatment slots.
sourceNotes: research/v2-3/src/internal/gamut-coverage.ts:166-181 defines ArtworkGamut.
provenanceNotes: The measurement binds the source raster and gamut policy.

artifactTypes.label: Gamut identity coverage scope
artifactTypes.description: Declared role scope, chromatic floor, hue window, saturation rule, field guard, slot count, and diagnostic-versus-objective use for gamut coverage.
sourceNotes: research/v4/MECHANISMS.md:1504-1507 requires declared scope and guards; gamut-coverage.ts:39-164 exposes the policy.
provenanceNotes: Objective contribution is explicit and may be diagnostic-only.

artifactTypes.label: Treatment gamut identity coverage
artifactTypes.description: Normalized whole-treatment chromatic coverage per internal treatment, with raw coverage, ceiling, saturation and field-guard decisions, and optional named objective contribution.
sourceNotes: research/v4/MECHANISMS.md:1504-1510 and gamut-coverage.ts:295-335 define normalized coverage and guards.
provenanceNotes: Coverage is a measurement over a named role scope, not a selected treatment.

artifactTypes.label: Incumbent internal treatment
artifactTypes.description: Canonical internal treatment and semantic identity to preserve unless an admitted challenger satisfies every replacement condition. This is not an exact v3 product Palette.
sourceNotes: research/v4/MECHANISMS.md:1521-1531 and NATIVE_COMPLETE_PALETTE_PROTOCOL.md:310-335 define canonical preservation.
provenanceNotes: Incumbent identity is input custody, not a product-anchor type.

artifactTypes.label: Canonical component-vector reconstruction
artifactTypes.description: Reconstruction state and, when available, the canonical named 27-component vector, five block decisions, evidence identities, and exact values. Unreconstructable is an explicit state with reasons.
sourceNotes: research/v4/MECHANISMS.md:1524-1531 and NATIVE_COMPLETE_PALETTE_PROTOCOL.md:310-323 require a reconstructable canonical vector and preserve canonical otherwise.
provenanceNotes: Unavailable components are not represented as zero or passing values.

artifactTypes.label: Treatment hard constraints
artifactTypes.description: Fixed complete-treatment legality constraints, check order, and epsilon semantics that every incumbent challenger must pass.
sourceNotes: research/v4/MECHANISMS.md:1521-1526 names hard constraints as explicit replacement input.
provenanceNotes: Constraint identity and frozen evaluation order are retained.

artifactTypes.label: Incumbent component bars
artifactTypes.description: Named absolute component thresholds, 27-component order, epsilon, changed-block classes, and candidate-to-candidate post-admission rules.
sourceNotes: research/v4/MECHANISMS.md:1522-1527 and NATIVE_COMPLETE_PALETTE_PROTOCOL.md:174-241, :316-333 define bars, vector order, epsilon, and post-admission selection.
provenanceNotes: No weighted compensation is encoded in this policy.

artifactTypes.label: Incumbent replacement report
artifactTypes.description: Hard and absolute-bar outcomes, componentwise domination certificate, admission set, minimum changed-block class, equality and incomparability reasons, and final unchanged-incumbent or replaced state.
sourceNotes: research/v4/MECHANISMS.md:1524-1531 requires the componentwise domination certificate and preservation reasons.
provenanceNotes: Exact equality, weaker components, incomparability, and unreconstructable canonical evidence are explicit unchanged states.

artifactTypes.label: Fixed treatment relaxation order
artifactTypes.description: Ordered legality forms and exact relaxations for field structure, gradient, collapse, and final black or white escape, including a stop condition after the final form.
sourceNotes: research/v4/MECHANISMS.md:1541-1546 and research/v3/phase-3/PROPOSAL_COMPARISON.md:9-21 require a fixed relaxation ladder and delayed escape.
provenanceNotes: Order is preference-bearing configuration and must not be inferred from iteration order.

artifactTypes.label: Treatment relaxation outcome
artifactTypes.description: Explicit first-nonempty or exhausted-still-infeasible state, selected legality form when present, ordered steps attempted, and resulting domain identity.

notes: The outcome discriminator records success at the first nonempty form or exhaustion of every configured form.
This is an inspection contract for the route outcome state, not a full decision payload schema.

sourceNotes: research/v4/MECHANISMS.md:1543-1546 requires first nonempty domain, legality form, and steps.
provenanceNotes: Failure to find a nonempty relaxed domain remains explicit infeasibility, not an absent output.

artifactTypes.label: Relaxation emptiness certificate
artifactTypes.description: Per-step proof and counts showing that every legality domain before the selected form was empty, or that every configured form remained empty or infeasible.
sourceNotes: research/v4/MECHANISMS.md:1543-1544 explicitly requires proof that earlier domains were empty.
provenanceNotes: Certificate scope is the supplied factors, legality settings, and relaxation order.

artifactTypes.label: Content tie-break policy
artifactTypes.description: Quantized quality-block order and resolution followed by ASCII complete-treatment content key, treatment ID, and structural key stages.
sourceNotes: research/v4/MECHANISMS.md:1555-1563 and candidate-materialization.ts:50-71 define the content-first deterministic stages.
provenanceNotes: Role hexes, gradient state, IDs, and structural labels used by the fallback are declared inputs to the policy.

artifactTypes.label: Published-shape internal treatment with midpoint
artifactTypes.description: Historical internal complete treatment paired with its actually published midpoint descriptor for bounded post-selection inspection. It is not the exact v3 Palette product contract.
sourceNotes: research/v2-3/src/internal/zero-contrast-repair.ts:118-133 defines PublishedPalette as internal treatment plus midpoint.
provenanceNotes: The midpoint descriptor travels with the treatment so a re-picked field cannot inherit the old midpoint.

artifactTypes.label: Ranked source-eligible repair slate
artifactTypes.description: Already evaluated source-eligible internal treatments with canonical key and rank, explicitly allowing an empty slate.
sourceNotes: research/v4/MECHANISMS.md:1577-1582 and zero-contrast-repair.ts:155-160 require a ranked source-eligible slate.
provenanceNotes: Repair may choose only from the supplied evaluated slate.

artifactTypes.label: Zero-contrast repair policy
artifactTypes.description: Explicit enforced and protected pair sets, raw readability bars, tier order, disturbance ordering, publish function identity, and disabled-empty configuration.
sourceNotes: research/v2-3/src/internal/zero-contrast-repair.ts:49-115, :247-261 makes enforced and protected sets explicit; empty enforced pairs means disabled.
provenanceNotes: Coverage and protection choices are data, not a hidden boolean.

artifactTypes.label: Internal repair result treatment
artifactTypes.description: The bounded repair result as an internal treatment, including byte-unchanged results and repaired alternatives. It is not the exact v3 product Palette and may be absent only for an explicit failed user-floor repick.
sourceNotes: research/v4/MECHANISMS.md:1575-1582 and :1592-1595 define bounded internal repair or repick results.
provenanceNotes: Outcome identity is carried separately so unchanged and unrepairable states are not inferred from value equality alone.

artifactTypes.label: Zero-contrast repair outcome
artifactTypes.description: Exactly one of unchanged-not-needed, swapped, same-field-slate, whole-slate-repicked, or unrepairable-unchanged, with incoming violations and protected-pair checks.
sourceNotes: research/v4/MECHANISMS.md:1577-1582 and zero-contrast-repair.ts:135-153 define all repair outcome states.
provenanceNotes: Unrepairable deliberately returns the original internal treatment unchanged.

artifactTypes.label: Requested user contrast floors
artifactTypes.description: Always-declared text and accent contrast requests with resolved effective floors and default identities for late feasibility filtering.
sourceNotes: research/v3/src/contract/types.ts:244-277 defines requested and resolved floors; PHASE_0_DECISIONS.md:154-157 requires default identity and zero collateral.
provenanceNotes: Floors filter an already evaluated order and do not alter generation or ranking.

artifactTypes.label: User-floor repick outcome
artifactTypes.description: Explicit byte-unchanged-valid, repicked-highest-ranked-valid, or failed-no-valid-alternative state with violated floors and selected rank when present.
sourceNotes: research/v4/MECHANISMS.md:1592-1597 requires unchanged, highest-ranked valid alternative, or declared failure.
provenanceNotes: Failure is explicit and does not authorize publishing below the requested floor.

notes: Traversal order is fixed for deterministic replay.

outputPorts.label: Objective-optimal internal treatment
valueStateNotes: Present only when the finite domain has a feasible optimum.
Absent for an empty or infeasible domain; the outcome and certificate remain present.

valueStateNotes: State is selected, empty-domain, or infeasible-domain.
notes: No selected treatment is represented by an explicit outcome.

outputPorts.label: Objective-relative optimality certificate
valueStateNotes: For a selected optimum, includes objective value and pruning proof.
For an empty domain, certifies emptiness relative to supplied factors.

censusStatus.statusText: scientific interpretation `supported` for observed loss from quantized dominance pruning and `inconclusive` as a sufficient retention rule; implementation state `historical`; evidence scope `complete-treatment`; runtime admissibility `permitted` only as a retention rule.

notes: The domain may be explicitly empty.

notes: Dimensions, directions, resolutions, and missing-value handling are frozen for the comparison.

outputPorts.label: Dominance partial order
valueStateNotes: An empty input produces an explicit empty partial order.
Incomparable pairs remain incomparable.

outputPorts.label: Retained Pareto subset
valueStateNotes: An empty input domain yields an empty frontier.
A nonempty finite domain retains every nondominated member.

outputPorts.label: Pareto membership and pruning audit
valueStateNotes: The empty-domain audit contains zero evaluation rows and explicit state.
notes: Includes each paretoMember flag and every audited pruned row.

censusStatus.statusText: scientific interpretation `inconclusive`; implementation state `historical`; evidence scope `mechanical` and `complete-treatment`; runtime admissibility `unresolved` as authority.

notes: An empty domain is orderable as an explicit empty sequence.

outputPorts.label: Banded total order
valueStateNotes: Empty input produces an explicit empty total order.
notes: This total order is distinct from Pareto dominance.

outputPorts.label: Evidence levels and deciding-stage trace
valueStateNotes: An empty order records no pairwise deciding stage.
notes: Includes quantized levels and tie-stage fallthrough.

notes: The domain carries constituent quality axes and may be empty.

valueStateNotes: An empty input produces an empty scalar-evaluation set.
notes: Constituent contributions remain inspectable.

outputPorts.label: Scalar quality total order
valueStateNotes: An empty input produces an explicit empty order.
notes: The order is tied to the declared exchange rates and does not assert general aesthetic authority.

inputPorts.label: Complete internal configurations
notes: The complete-configuration domain may be empty.

inputPorts.label: Global coding model
notes: Role, collapse, gradient, and data-fit prices are model inputs.

outputPorts.label: Minimum-cost internal treatment
valueStateNotes: Absent when the supplied configuration domain is empty.
notes: The selected value is internal and relative to the tested coding model.

outputPorts.label: MDL selection outcome
valueStateNotes: State is selected or empty-domain.
notes: An explicit outcome accompanies optional selection.

outputPorts.label: Cost and coding breakdown
valueStateNotes: An empty input records no optimum and zero evaluated configurations.
notes: Contains costs and explanation breakdown for every evaluated configuration.

inputPorts.label: Rival complete-treatment portfolio
notes: The portfolio may explicitly contain no members.

inputPorts.label: Member-independent evidence
notes: Evidence does not use extractor identity as a feature.

outputPorts.label: Selected internal portfolio member
valueStateNotes: Absent for an empty portfolio or an explicit no-election result.
notes: This selector output is not the exact v3 product palette.

outputPorts.label: Portfolio election outcome
valueStateNotes: State is selected, empty-portfolio, or no-election.
